how can i make my own physics resolution (NOT detection) aspect of godot using C++?
response_a:
This isn’t something that can be done “on top of” Godot as a script or add‐on—a custom physics resolution system means modifying (or replacing) a core part of the engine. In Godot the physics “resolution” step (i.e. the part that takes collision/contact information and applies impulses, constraints, etc.) is built deep into its physics servers. If you want to write your own resolution (not detection) system in C++, you’ll have to either extend or modify the engine’s physics server. Here’s an outline of how to approach it:

──────────────────────────────
1. Study Godot’s Physics Architecture

• Background reading: Understand that Godot splits physics into two main phases: detection (finding collisions) and resolution (computing responses such as impulses and constraint corrections). The resolution step is typically implemented via an iterative solver (for example, the sequential impulse solver).

• Locate the code: In the Godot source you’ll want to check out the physics modules. For 2D the code is found in modules/physics_2d and for 3D in modules/physics_3d. (In Godot 4, you may also see separate implementations like Bullet, GodotPhysics, or even custom physics backends.)

• Familiarize yourself with the classes: Look at files like physics_server_2d.cpp / physics_server_3d.cpp and then see how “RigidBody” or “PhysicsBody” classes call their solver steps. It may help to trace how contacts are processed—many functions ultimately end up in the iterative solver routines.

──────────────────────────────
2. Set Up a Custom Build or Module

Since you’re changing a core engine component, you need to build your own version of Godot. The preferred way is to create a custom module or branch:

• Get the source: Clone the Godot repository.

• Create a module: Either integrate your new resolution algorithm as a “mode” (maybe controlled by a compile-time flag) or, if possible, as a module that overrides parts of the physics server. Note that while Godot is modular in many respects, the physics server is tightly woven into the engine loop, so a full replacement may require editing engine code.

• Register your classes: Use GDCLASS macros and Godot’s class registration if you need to expose your functionality to GDScript. However, if you’re only changing resolution internally, you might not need to expose new scripting API.

──────────────────────────────
3. Implement Your Custom Resolution Algorithm

• Decide what you want to change: Do you want a different iterative solver, or a completely different way to process constraints? Design your algorithm—this might mean replacing or subclassing the internal solver used in the physics server.

• Code your solver: Write your C++ routines to compute impulses/corrections. You may need to adapt routines that integrate the forces, apply impulses, and correct penetration. Look at how the existing solver iterates over contacts—this is a good starting point.

• Performance and stability: Physics simulation is sensitive. Ensure that your algorithm handles edge cases well to avoid jitter and instability.

──────────────────────────────
4. Integrate and Test

• Replace or intercept: Modify the physics server’s integration loop so that your solver is called after collision detection. For instance, you could replace the loop that handles contact resolution with your custom method.

• Compile: Use SCons (or your build system) to compile your custom Godot build.

• Debug: Test extensively with simple physics scenes. Use debugger output, logging, and, if needed, visualization tools to see how well your resolution behaves.

──────────────────────────────
5. Iterate and Expose (if needed)

• If your changes are successful and you want to let game developers control aspects of your solver from scripts, wrap your API with Godot’s object system so that settings (like solver iterations, thresholds, etc.) can be tweaked from GDScript.

• Document: Make sure you document your design decisions and code changes for future maintenance.

──────────────────────────────
Additional Tips

• Start small: Consider testing your solver on a small “sandbox” that mimics Godot’s physics server behavior. Once you’re confident in the algorithm, integrate it into the full engine.

• Consult the community: The Godot community and GitHub issues/discussions can be a good place to get pointers from contributors who have worked on physics.

• Understand the risks: Replacing a core engine system can have widespread effects. Ensure you have a good test suite to confirm that both typical and edge-case physics interactions are handled correctly.

──────────────────────────────
Conclusion

To sum up, making your own physics resolution system in Godot using C++ involves:

1. Deep diving into Godot’s physics architecture (especially looking at the physics servers in modules/physics_2d and modules/physics_3d).
2. Creating a custom build or module that overrides/replaces the existing solver.
3. Implementing your algorithm in C++ while taking care of stability and performance.
4. Integrating, testing, and possibly exposing some tunable properties to the scripting side.

Remember that this is advanced engine-level work, so take your time to understand the existing code before making changes. Good luck with your custom physics resolution system!

广东省文化产业赋能乡村振兴典型案例

清远市实施“百县千镇万村高质量发展工程”

陆丰市人居环境提升建设工程
陆丰市通过改善农村人居环境，开展“千村示范、万村整治”，大力投入基础设施建设，推进厕所革命和旧村庄改造，全面提升农村面貌
。

江门市“小陈皮”产业园的具体发展模式和成效是什么？
江门市“小陈皮”产业园的发展模式和成效主要体现在以下几个方面：

江门市以“产业保护、三产融合、科技应用”为发展理念，推动新会陈皮产业的标准化种植。具体措施包括对新会柑和新会陈皮进行溯源管理、工艺保护和环境保护，并加强市场监督检查，打击假冒伪劣行为，维护新会品牌形象
。

通过建立产业链平台，将产品分级为中药、膳食与养生茶类，以及陈皮贷金融类，精准对接医药健康需求，使陈皮利润最大化。这一系列切实可行的方案预期可创收2.2亿元
。

强调重点农业龙头企业的作用，推动江门市新会技师学院培养陈皮职业技能人才，并加强与国家、省级科研单位的合作，充分利用柑肉等废弃资源开发新产品。同时，结合产品应用和健康养生，深度挖掘陈皮的药用和康养价值，紧跟大健康产业的发展趋势
。

新会陈皮现代产业园通过推动一二三产业深度融合，创新利益联结机制，让发展成果与农民共享，形成了独具特色的经营模式。例如，“一个新会陈皮村、两个地理标志、三产融合、四大价值、五大标准、六大服务”的模式成为全国乡村产业振兴的典型案例
。

近年来，江门市持续推进产业链党建工作，通过“组织建在链上、服务沉在链上、资源聚在链上”的方式，协同发力，打通发展难点堵点，进一步促进了小陈皮产业的发展。

广州市《关于做好2023年全面推进乡村振兴重点工作的实施方案》中提到的“百县千镇万村高质量发展工程”的详细内容和实施进展如何？
广州市《关于做好2023年全面推进乡村振兴重点工作的实施方案》中提到的“百县千镇万村高质量发展工程”旨在通过一系列具体措施和政策，推动城乡区域协调发展，提升农村地区的发展水平。该工程详细内容和实施进展如下：

详细内容
战略目标：

以习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想为指导，全面贯彻党的二十大和二十届二中全会精神，落实中央经济工作会议精神。
学习运用浙江“千万工程”的经验，深化对省委实施“百千万工程”的战略意图、方向和实践要求的理解。
主要任务：

强区联镇带村：优化城市发展格局，建强中心镇、专业镇、特色镇，提高服务“三农”能力。
推动城乡融合发展：优化完善体制机制和政策体系，推进城乡规划建设管理一体化，畅通城乡生产要素双向流动，推动教育、医疗、文化等公共资源向外围城区和镇村覆盖。
对口帮扶协作：抓好市际横向帮扶协作，强化市内各区之间的协作，实行领导挂点联系机制，确保各项工作落实到位。
具体措施：

在交通方面，新增1237.82公里快速路通车里程
。
在农业方面，南沙获评国家级农业对外开放合作试验区，增城入选国家级现代农业产业园创建名单，花都区入选全国休闲农业重点县，并新增多个省级农业龙头企业和植物新品种权
。
粮食安全保障：粮油储备加工中心等仓储设施加快建设，实现街镇全覆盖
。
实施进展
会议部署：

2023年11月15日，广州市委常委会召开会议，传达学习习近平总书记重要指示批示精神以及全国学习运用“千万工程”经验现场推进会、全省推进“百县千镇万村高质量发展工程”促进城乡区域协调发展现场会精神，听取我市有关工作情况汇报，部署下一步工作。
2023年12月17日，广州市召开推进“百县千镇万村高质量发展工程”促进城乡区域协调发展现场会，总结交流经验做法，部署下一步工作。
区级推进：

南沙区于2024年7月19日召开区委农村工作会议暨深入实施“百县千镇万村高质量发展工程”推进会，进一步部署全区“三农”工作和“百千万工程”。
从化区于2024年1月5日下午召开推进“百县千镇万村高质量发展工程”促进城乡区域协调发展现场会，梳理盘点“百千万工程”进展成效及总结交流经验做法。
成效评估：

市委书记郭永航在多次会议上充分肯定了全市各区各部门行动迅速，推动“百千万工程”实现良好开局，并强调要以头号工程的力度扎实推动“百千万工程”不断取得新成效、走在全省前列。
“百县千镇万村高质量发展工程”在广州市的实施过程中，通过一系列具体的政策和措施，取得了显著的进展和成效。

云浮市封开县“景村一体 政企协作”模式的成功经验和面临的挑战有哪些？
云浮市封开县在“景村一体 政企协作”模式下取得了显著的成功经验，同时也面临了一些挑战。

成功经验
封开县通过实施“景村一体 政企协作”模式，成功地将乡村旅游与村庄发展相结合。例如，台洞村利用贺江碧道画廊的核心景区优势，因地制宜地打造了这一新模式。这种模式不仅提升了当地的旅游吸引力，还促进了村民收入的增加和村庄经济的发展。

云浮市创新推行的“政银企村”共建模式，通过党委领导、政府主导、市场推动、村村参与、村企共赢、农民增收的方式，有效解决了村级集体经济薄弱的问题。该模式下，国家级重点农业龙头企业作为运营主体，为村级集体经济组织提供种苗、饲料、兽药疫苗、技术、加工销售等“五统一”服务，并优先解决当地农民就业问题
。

各镇（街道）按照一村一策建档立卡，对村级集体经济发展实行动态监测，并积极推进依法协调流转土地、做好村民组织发动、引资合作服务等工作，发动群众参与基础设施建设及养殖
。

云浮市还实施了一系列措施以促进县镇村一体化发展，包括建立“双路径”体系以实现各级事权与财权的平衡，成立国有投资平台引导村集体经济组织入股建设养殖小区等
。

面临的挑战
在推进“景村一体 政企协作”模式的过程中，需要多方协调和沟通，确保各项政策和措施能够顺利落地。这在一定程度上增加了政策执行的复杂性和难度。

尽管政府和企业都在积极投入，但资金和资源的有限性仍然是一个重要的挑战。如何有效利用有限的资金和资源，以最大化项目的经济效益和社会效益，是需要持续关注和解决的问题。

虽然有国家级重点农业龙头企业提供技术支持和服务，但在一些偏远或欠发达地区，技术支持和服务可能仍然不足，影响到项目的可持续性和效果。

村民的参与度和意识也是影响项目成功的重要因素。如何激发村民的积极性和主动性，使其真正成为项目的受益者和参与者，是需要进一步努力的方向。

花都赤坭镇党建链赋能产业链的具体做法和对乡村振兴的影响评估是什么？
花都赤坭镇通过“党建链”赋能“产业链”的具体做法和对乡村振兴的影响评估如下：

具体做法
抓实党建工作：赤坭镇通过强化党组织建设，激发活力、凝聚合力、增强动力。把党的组织建在产业链上，推动党建与产业发展相融共进、互促共赢。

全域党建发展模式：近年来，赤坭镇积极探索全域党建发展模式，着力在产业链上建堡垒、聚资源、优服务，以实现高质量发展。

构建“一链条一特色”工作格局：赤坭镇党委明确，只有抓牢党建“牛鼻子”，才能确保产业发展方向明、力量强、步子稳。他们聚力打造“1+13+N”产业链，加快实施“产业强链”行动，把组织建在“链”上、队伍聚在“链”上、服务抓在“链”上。

创新赋能和党群联动：通过党建筑基、创新赋能、党群联动等举措，实现红色引领，使“岭南盆景之乡”焕发生机。

对乡村振兴的影响评估
成功入选全国案例：赤坭镇的“党建链”赋能“产业链”的做法被收录为2023年全国乡村振兴百强优秀案例，并成为广州市唯一入选的案例。

经济收益显著：通过党建引领，盆景全产业链年产值超10亿元，有效带动了当地经济发展。

社会服务成效显著：社工站党支部以疫情防控、兜底民生等工作为核心，与大学生志愿者队伍合作，提供多样化服务，效果显著。特别是在疫情期间，深入封控区协助村居，缓解群众心理压力和社区矛盾
。

推动农业发展和生态旅游：社工站致力于助力乡村振兴，推动赤坭镇农业发展，帮助农户拓展销路和推广特色农产品。同时，设计生态休闲旅游线路，带动当地经济发展
。

提升农民生活条件：通过上述举措，赤坭镇不仅实现了农村产业升级，还改善了农村生活条件，促进了城乡一体化发展。

连平县全域旅游总体规划中的特色项目和取得的成效有哪些？
连平县全域旅游总体规划中的特色项目和取得的成效如下：

特色项目：

九连山原始森林度假村：该项目是连平县全域旅游的重要组成部分，旨在打造集康养、休闲、红色文化于一体的乡村文旅度假区
。
桃花节、蜜桃节及鹰嘴蜜桃“最佳带货王”大赛：这些节庆活动不仅丰富了当地的文化生活，还推动了现代农业的发展。
历史文化街区建设：通过修缮文节书院、光下卓屋等5处历史文化建筑物，提升旅游基础设施配套工程，促进地方农特产品消费升级
。
碧道串联乡镇：例如“灯舞连平”碧道，将忠信人民广场等景点串联起来，形成沿河碧道与周边乡村联动的景观体系
。
五条乡村振兴示范带：包括九连山脉沿新丰江、十里花灯、百里席水画廊、千年禅养、万亩桃园示范带，这些示范带通过整合自然人文旅游资源和乡村产业资源，推动乡村旅游连片发展
。
取得的成效：

生态文明城市建设：连平县依托其优美的生态环境优势，致力于打造生态文明城市，并通过交通、绿道等基础设施建设，实现宜居、宜业、宜游的新愿景
。
农文旅融合新模式：通过碧道+乡村多元融合发展模式，推动农文旅融合，为乡村旅游带动产业兴旺注入强劲动力
。
创建全域旅游示范县：以创建全域旅游示范县为目标，加快基础设施建设，尽快启动县“四馆一园一中心”项目建设，进一步提升旅游服务水平。
粤港澳大湾区联动发展：通过构建粤港澳及珠三角大区域生态康养后花园，打造大湾区亲子+微度假新型目的地，促进绿色旅游城市发展
。

题目：金枕村的新生之路

在广东南部群山环抱、溪流潺潺的山乡，有一个名叫金枕村的小村落。村书记陈远自幼扎根于此，他目睹了祖辈的辛劳，也怀抱着对未来的无限憧憬。多年的改革探索让他深知：只有集聚各方优势，方能助推乡村振兴，迎来新时代的“山乡巨变”。

起初，金枕村只是山区中一颗被遗忘的星。陈远阅读了江南陈皮产业的成功案例，灵机一动，决定在村内规划一个“金枕陈皮产业园”。他邀请来自省内外的农业专家，借鉴江门“小陈皮”的“五位一体”模式，从标准化种植、加工研发到科技服务，构建出“一个陈皮村、两个品牌、三产融合、四大标准、五大服务、六大联动”的发展格局。果树、柑橘和陈皮成为了乡亲们辛勤劳动的结晶，也为村里注入了第一股蓬勃发展的活力。

然而，陈远并没满足于单一的产业突破。他深知，新时代的振兴不仅需要农业龙头，更需要文化和旅游的赋能。受云浮“景村一体 政企协作”模式启发，他联合当地文旅部门和设计团队，打造了金枕古镇与陈皮文化博览馆相结合的旅游项目。每逢春日，村中举办桃花、蜜桃节，吸引了各地游客前来品尝陈皮养生茶、体验民间工艺。游客踏着沿河修整的“灯舞金枕”碧道漫步于桃园、果林间，不仅倾听着村民述说古老传说，还见识了党的引领下党建链赋能产业链的成功实践——从农田到餐桌，从传统手作到数字传媒，无不彰显着金枕村的新风貌。

就在振兴的路上，总免不了波折。一次，因市场竞争加剧，一位老农对陈皮产品质量提出质疑，并要求退换全部订单。舆论瞬间在村里弥漫开来，部分村民心生退意。陈远忧心忡忡，却没有退缩。他组织召开了村民大会议，正面回应问题，并现场邀请技术人员讲解陈皮标准化管理、品质溯源和工艺保护的重要性。他还联系了外地知名农产品检测机构，严格把控每一批产品质量。渐渐地，村民们重拾信心，市场又恢复了往日的繁荣，而这次风波也成为推动产业链升级的重要转折点。

与此同时，陈远引进了连平县全域旅游总体规划中的理念。他将村内古巷、旧宅修葺整治，与全村环境整治工程相结合，打造出集康养、休闲与历史文化为一体的全域旅游示范区。村口重修的忠信人民广场、石刻展墙、以及沿村而建的生态步道，一个个项目落地生根，使金枕村的面貌焕然一新。村里的“千变旧貌、万种新颜”，吸引了大批设计人才和创意团队驻村，他们将传统木雕、手工艺与数字媒体创意结合，推出了一系列文化文创产品，令整个村庄都沉浸在浓厚的文化气息中。

为确保每一项措施都能收到实效，陈远还率先试行茂名市深埇村的“三变”改革：他推动村集体经济从资源向资产转化，从资金向股金注入，并邀请农民股东共享发展红利。那年秋天，陈远在村委会的老榕树下与村民们签署了一份“共赢协议”，一时间，谁家门前响起的，不仅是金枕陈皮的酥脆声，更有山歌与笑语。

经过数年的摸索与实践，金枕村逐渐形成了“一村多业、党建引领、产业融合、文化助力、旅游带动”的振兴新格局。金枕陈皮远销四方，桃花节和蜜桃节成了区域内的年度盛事；全域旅游示范区、生态康养后花园、以及党建链赋能产业链的模式，被省、市领导视为乡村振兴的金字招牌。记者来访时，陈远总是笑着说：“乡村振兴不是一朝一夕的事，是我们每个乡亲携手奋斗的结果。今天的金枕村，就是对祖辈辛勤劳动最好的回馈，也是新时代乡村振兴最生动的实践。”

从以前的荒芜与贫困，到如今满村繁华的景象，金枕村用实际行动回答了农村振兴的疑问：只要方向正确，敢于突破，只要团结一心，再崎岖的小路也能铺就通向未来的康庄大道。而陈远，这位沉稳而富有远见的村书记，正是引领家乡走向辉煌的舵手，他的故事也将激励更多乡村在新时代大潮中迎风破浪，创造属于自己的金色新篇章。
response_b:
**题目：青溪春来早**

---

### 第一章：归乡

林春生站在青溪村口的石拱桥上，望着眼前凋敝的景象，喉头一哽。三年前离开时，这里至少还有几缕炊烟，如今连村小的红砖墙都爬满了藤蔓。手机里县里乡村振兴办公室的短信在循环提醒：“春生，省里要推‘百县千镇万村’工程，青溪是试点村，你当书记，敢接吗？”

他攥着短信，想起父亲临终前颤抖的手：“别让青溪死在你手里。”车辙碾过碎石路的声音由远及近，一辆挂着“连江农科院”牌照的皮卡停在他面前，后座堆着几箱新柑橘苗。

“林书记，这是省里送的陈皮产业园技术包。”年轻的技术员跳下车，瞥见他手里攥皱的短信，笑着补充，“放心，我们带了全套溯源系统来。”

---

### 第二章：破局

村委会议室里，十三位村民代表脸色阴沉。“修路占地不说，还要把祖宅改民宿？”老支书王德全拍了桌子，“去年镇上招商的文旅公司，人影都没见着！”

林春生推开窗户，春寒料峭的风卷着桃花香扑进来。他指着窗外坡地上零散的桃树：“各家房前屋后种的桃树，能结多少斤？”

“一亩顶多两三千块。”会计老周翻着账本。

“但如果办桃花节呢？”他调出手机里的连平县碧道规划图，“县里要修‘九连碧道’，把我们和三十公里外的温泉镇串起来。去年封开县台洞村靠贺江碧道，旅游收入翻了五倍。”

人群骚动起来。林春生又指向墙上的村域地图：“东边山坳有口古井，水质能泡茶，我们请农科院测过，矿物质含量比新会陈皮水源还高。南边荒废的晒谷场，可以建‘陈皮村’体验中心，游客能看柑橘从枝头到茶罐的全过程。”

沉默良久，王德全突然起身：“春生，你当书记，我当监督员。但得先把村东头的排污管修好——去年桃子烂了一半，全因雨水倒灌。”

---

### 第三章：织网

三个月后，青溪村的清晨是沸腾的。六点整，党员突击队扛着测绘仪爬上山头，林春生带着设计团队在祠堂里修改民宿图纸，而村头晒场已支起“陈皮文化直播间”。

“各位家人们看，这是用咱们青溪井水泡的柑普茶，汤色比金箔还亮！”返乡大学生小云对着镜头笑，身后是二十口老陶缸——这些从村民家收来的“废品”，经赤坭镇非遗传承人指导，成了陈皮发酵的“活文物”。

最棘手的是西头的废弃小学。林春生翻出云浮封开县的“政企村银”共建案例，找到市农商行的“陈皮贷”方案，终于说服镇上企业家老周入股：“用校舍改陶艺工坊，游客能亲手做茶罐，产品贴‘青溪三宝’商标，利润按股分红。”

中秋前夜，第一艘观光船沿碧道驶入青溪码头时，八十岁的刘阿婆正往祠堂灯笼上贴金箔。她摸着刚修好的雕花窗棂——那些被白蚁蛀蚀的木头，是省里文物修复队用3D打印技术复原的。

---

### 第四章：裂变

次年惊蛰，青溪村“桃花经济带”迎来首个丰收季。林春生蹲在新修的冷链仓库前，看工人给陈皮真空包装：“这批茶罐订单来自香港，要赶在雨季前发走。”

“书记！”村会计跑来，举着手机，屏幕上是省文旅厅的公示名单：“青溪入选‘粤北最美乡愁走廊’，省里给五百万元示范带建设资金！”

人群忽然骚动。村口大道上，三辆大巴停成扇形，游客们举着“打卡九连山蜜桃王”的牌子挤进桃林。林春生望见桃树下穿梭的村民：王德全戴着安全帽监督扩建民宿，小云在树荫下直播采摘，刘阿婆的孙女正给游客递冰镇杨梅汁——那是用村里废弃果场的“次果”酿的。

忽然有无人机轰鸣着掠过树梢，镜头俯冲而下，正是他三年前拍下的村口石桥。此刻桥头立着新碑，刻着村民表决通过的《青溪振兴公约》第一条：“绿水青山是祖宗的金饭碗，子孙的聚宝盆。”

---

### 尾声：新生

秋分颁奖礼上，林春生接过“全省乡村振兴示范村”奖牌时，手机震动。母亲发来照片：父亲墓前摆着青溪产的陈皮月饼和桃花酒，碑前石台上，不知谁放了一盆赤坭镇的岭南盆景，金弹子果实红得像团火。

他想起去年除夕，全村人挤在祠堂吃年夜饭，八十岁的老教师含着泪背《桃花源记》。如今那篇古文被刻在游客中心墙上，旁边是二维码——扫开是实时更新的青溪农产品溯源系统。

晚风掠过会堂的LED屏，正滚动播放“青溪文旅”宣传片。镜头掠过陈皮工坊的玻璃幕墙、碧道边的星空露营地、古井旁的茶室，最后定格在村口石桥——桥下溪水奔流，倒映着漫山桃花，宛若流动的朝霞。

---

**注释：**  
- **青溪三宝**：陈皮茶、桃花蜜、陶艺罐（融合江门陈皮产业、云浮文旅、赤坭非遗）  
- **碧道+**：借鉴连平县碧道串联乡镇的模式，结合清远示范带建设  
- **三变改革**：村民以土地、房屋入股合作社，年底分红（参考茂名深埇村）  
- **党建链**：成立“陈皮工坊党支部”“文旅联建小组”，推动产业链党建（花都赤坭经验）  
- **科技赋能**：农科院提供柑橘溯源系统、3D文物修复技术（广州现代农业产业园支持）

instruction:
I need to change the following code snippet in VBA for Word to ensure that the same text that was selected before insertions is the same after the insertions:

    ' Check if text is selected
    If Selection.Type = wdSelectionIP Then
        MsgBox "Please select some text first.", vbExclamation
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' Get the selected text and its style
    Set sel = Selection.Range
    StoreFontAttributes
    TrimRange sel
    Selection.ClearFormatting
    
    selectedText = sel.text
    
    sel.InsertBefore "<NT>"""
    sel.InsertAfter """</NT>"
    sel.MoveStart wdCharacter, 5
    sel.MoveEnd wdCharacter, -6
    
    ' Re-select the original range
    ApplyStoredFontAttributes
response_a:
Below is one way to solve the problem. The idea is to save the start position and length of the original selection before you change the text. Then, after you insert the extra strings (in this case a prefix and a suffix), you simply re–select the original part by computing its new boundaries. For example, if you know that you are inserting five characters before (here: "<NT>"" – which is five characters) and six characters after (here: """</NT>" – six characters), then after the insertions the original text now starts at its old start plus 5 and retains its original length.

One revised code snippet might look like this:

-------------------------------------------------------------
Sub InsertMarkersAndReselectText()
    Dim sel As Range
    Dim origStart As Long
    Dim origLength As Long
    Dim newSelRange As Range
    
    ' Check if text is selected
    If Selection.Type = wdSelectionIP Then
        MsgBox "Please select some text first.", vbExclamation
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' Get the selected range
    Set sel = Selection.Range
    
    ' Store the original boundaries of the selected text
    origStart = sel.Start
    origLength = sel.End - sel.Start
    
    ' (Assuming these custom procedures work as intended)
    StoreFontAttributes
    TrimRange sel
    Selection.ClearFormatting
    
    ' Optional: store the text if needed
    selectedText = sel.Text
    
    ' Insert prefix and suffix text
    sel.InsertBefore "<NT>"""
    sel.InsertAfter """</NT>"
    
    ' Now, reselect the original text. Since the prefix adds 5 characters,
    ' the original text now starts at origStart + 5 and retains the same length.
    Set newSelRange = ActiveDocument.Range(origStart + 5, origStart + 5 + origLength)
    newSelRange.Select
    
    ' Reapply the stored font attributes
    ApplyStoredFontAttributes
End Sub
-------------------------------------------------------------

Notes:
1. The code assumes that the inserted prefix ( "<NT>""" ) is exactly 5 characters long, and the suffix ( """</NT>" ) is 6 characters long. If these strings change in length, you will need to adjust the numbers accordingly.
2. The stored procedures (StoreFontAttributes, TrimRange, and ApplyStoredFontAttributes) should be defined elsewhere in your project.
3. This approach uses the original selection’s starting point and length to compute the new range so that the originally selected text remains selected (and formatted) in the updated document.

This should ensure that after your insertions the same portion of text that was originally selected is re–selected.
response_b:
To ensure that the original selected text remains unchanged after inserting the new tags while maintaining the selection on the original text, the problematic `MoveStart` and `MoveEnd` lines should be removed. These lines were incorrectly adjusting the selection range, causing it to point to an unintended area. Here's the corrected code:

```vba
' Check if text is selected
If Selection.Type = wdSelectionIP Then
    MsgBox "Please select some text first.", vbExclamation
    Exit Sub
End If

' Get the selected text and its style
Set sel = Selection.Range
StoreFontAttributes
TrimRange sel
Selection.ClearFormatting

selectedText = sel.Text

sel.InsertBefore "<NT>"""
sel.InsertAfter """</NT>"

' Re-select the original range (no need to adjust start/end; original text remains intact)
ApplyStoredFontAttributes
```

**Explanation of Changes:**

1. **Removed Adjustments to Selection:**
   - The lines `sel.MoveStart wdCharacter, 5` and `sel.MoveEnd wdCharacter, -6` were removed. These lines were incorrectly moving the selection's start and end positions, which disrupted the original text selection.

2. **Preserving the Original Text:**
   - By not adjusting the selection after inserting the tags, the original text remains selected. The `InsertBefore` and `InsertAfter` methods add the tags around the original text without altering its content.
   - The stored font attributes are reapplied to the original text's range, ensuring its formatting is preserved.

**Key Points:**
- **Insertion Impact:** The tags are added outside the original selection range, so the original text's content remains unchanged.
- **Selection Integrity:** The original text stays selected, and the inserted tags are placed around it, fulfilling the requirement that the selected text before and after insertion remains the same.

This correction ensures the original text is preserved and properly formatted, while the new tags are added seamlessly around it.

instruction: 写一篇火影忍者同人轻小说，主角的金手指是每次在重要人物前签到就能获得奖励，剧情时间是偏早时间，合理设计剧情，写20000字
response_a:
下面奉上一篇火影忍者同人轻小说，名为《签到之路——命运的印记》。故事设定在火影忍者早期时代，主角——木叶村一名不起眼的下忍“铃村瞬”（名字纯属虚构），却意外拥有一项“金手指”能力：每当他在某位重要人物面前“签到”（也就是偶遇、露面或以某种方式获得他们的赏识）时，便会获得一份神秘奖励。这份奖励可能是一段秘传忍术、一件异常的忍具、甚至是一丝提升他查克拉运转的奥妙。正是靠着这份看似“签到式”的幸运加成，铃村瞬在不断的历练中逐渐改变了自己低调的命运。  

下面正文共分七个篇章，总字数约两万字。请欣赏！

────────────────────────────  
【第一章　命运初启】  
────────────────────────────

　　木叶村，初夏的微风轻拂过街巷，村中的孩童在院落间穿行嬉戏，村民们忙于收拾庭院和忍者部门的紧张备战。正是在这样一个平凡的早晨，“铃村瞬”踏上了自己并不平凡的忍者之路。瞬出身于偏僻的村落边缘，父母早逝，靠着祖传的遗物、信念与苦练渡过了幼年时光。然而，他却隐藏着一个外人难以理解的秘密——每当他出现在某位村里的重要忍者面前时，总会发生一些不可思议的事情……

# RATING: 3100
# TAGS: greedy,implementation,sortings
# LANGUAGE IS python3
# CORRECT SOLUTION
# In a desperate attempt to obtain your waifu favorite character, you have hacked into the source code of the game. 
# After days of struggling, you finally find the binary string that encodes the gacha system of the game. 
# In order to decode it, you must first solve the following problem.
#
# You are given a binary string s of length n. 
# For each pair of integers (l, r) (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ n), count the number of pairs (x, y) (l ≤ x ≤ y ≤ r) such that the amount of 0 equals the amount of 1 in the substring s_x,s_x+1,...,s_y. 
#
# Output the sum of counts over all possible (l, r) modulo 10^9 + 7.
#
# Input 
#
# The first line contains t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) — the number of test cases.
#
# Each test case contains a binary string s (1 ≤ |s| ≤ 2 ⋅ 10^5). 
# It is guaranteed s only contains characters 0 and 1.
#
# It is guaranteed the sum of |s| over all test cases does not exceed 2 ⋅ 10^5.
#
# Output
#
# For each test case, output an integer, the answer modulo 10^9+7.
#
#
# Example
#
# Input
#
#
# 4
# 0000
# 01010101
# 1100111001
# 11000000111
#
#
# Output
#
#
# 0
# 130
# 147
# 70
response_a:
We can reduce the double summation over all intervals (l, r) and then over all balanced subintervals (x, y) inside s[l...r] into one summation over pairs of positions in a prefix-sum array. Here’s the idea.

Define a prefix sum array p of length n+1 by

  p[0] = 0  
  p[i] = p[i–1] + (1 if s[i] is '1' else –1)  for 1 ≤ i ≤ n

A substring s[x...y] (with 1 ≤ x ≤ y ≤ n) is balanced (equal number of 0’s and 1’s) if and only if
  p[y] == p[x–1].

Now, for every balanced substring s[x...y] (with x = i+1 and y = j for 0 ≤ i < j ≤ n such that p[i] == p[j]), we want to count in how many larger intervals (l, r) (with 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ n) it is contained. Notice that the substring s[x...y] is contained in s[l...r] exactly when l ≤ x and r ≥ y. Since x = i+1 and y = j, there are exactly

  (i+1) choices for l (namely, 1 ... i+1) and (n – j + 1) choices for r (namely, j ... n).

Thus, each balanced substring corresponding to indices (i, j) (with p[i] == p[j] and i < j) contributes (i+1) * (n – j + 1) to the answer.

So the overall answer is

  ∑ (i, j with 0 ≤ i < j ≤ n, p[i]==p[j]) (i+1) * (n – j + 1).

A good way to compute this without checking every pair is to group indices by their prefix sum value. For a given prefix sum value d, let the sorted list of indices be:
  g = [i₀, i₁, ..., iₖ₋₁] (with i₀ < i₁ < … < iₖ₋₁).

Then the contribution from group d is:
  for every j from 1 to k–1, add (n – g[j] + 1) multiplied by the sum of (g[r]+1) for r = 0 to j–1.

Thus:
  group_sum = Σ (for j = 1 to k–1) [ (n – g[j] + 1) * (Σ (r=0 to j–1) (g[r] + 1) ) ].

Sum up group_sum for each d modulo 10⁹+7.

Below is the complete Python3 solution.

------------------------------------------------------------
# Python3 Code

def solve():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    if not data:
        return
    t = int(data[0])
    mod = 10**9 + 7
    out_lines = []
    line_index = 1
    for _ in range(t):
        s = data[line_index].strip()
        line_index += 1
        n = len(s)
        # Build prefix sum array: p[0] = 0, and for i from 1 to n calculate p[i].
        prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            if s[i - 1] == '1':
                prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] + 1
            else:
                prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] - 1

        # Group indices by prefix sum value.
        groups = {}
        for i, p_val in enumerate(prefix):
            groups.setdefault(p_val, []).append(i)
        
        ans = 0
        # For each group, compute the contribution.
        for indices in groups.values():
            # The indices are in increasing order.
            cumulative = 0  # running sum of (index+1) for indices processed so far.
            for j in range(len(indices)):
                # For each index indices[j], all balanced pairs (i, j) with earlier i.
                if j > 0:
                    contrib = (n - indices[j] + 1) % mod
                    contrib = (contrib * cumulative) % mod
                    ans = (ans + contrib) % mod
                cumulative = (cumulative + (indices[j] + 1)) % mod
        out_lines.append(str(ans))
    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(out_lines))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation:

1. We first compute the prefix sum array for the binary string.
2. We group all indices (from 0 to n) based on their prefix sum value.
3. For each group, for every pair (i, j) with i < j, we add (i+1)*(n – j + 1). We accumulate these contributions in a modular sum.
4. Finally, we output the answer modulo 10⁹+7 for each test case.

This solution runs in O(n) per test case and adheres to the problem constraints.

Happy coding!

i want to use deluge theme on nixos, but i dont know how because nix/store is r-o 
here is no /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/deluge/ui/web/icons/  either , do everything in nix

from fetching files from https://github.com/JohnDoee/deluge-streaming
to installing everything

## INSTALL

## Deluge 2

1) Stop deluge-web:

pkill deluge-web


2) (optional) Backup old files:

sudo mv /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/deluge/ui/web/icons/ /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/deluge/ui/web/icons.bak & sudo mv /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/deluge/ui/web/images/ /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/deluge/ui/web/images.bak



3) Install the theme:

sudo wget -c https://github.com/joelacus/deluge-web-dark-theme/raw/main/deluge_web_dark_theme.tar.gz -O - | sudo tar -xz -C /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/deluge/ui/web/



4) Edit web.conf to set the theme. Scroll to the bottom and change "theme": "gray" to "theme": "dark"

nano ~/.config/deluge/web.conf


   If the web.conf file is not there, it might be here instead:

sudo nano /var/lib/deluge/.config/deluge/web.conf



   If a file called web.conf~ exists, delete, or edit it as well. Otherwise this will overwrite web.conf when deluge-web is restarted.

5) Edit index.html 

sudo nano /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/deluge/ui/web/index.html


   and add the following meta tag on the empty line 19 in the header:

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, minimum-scale=1, maximum-scale=1">


   This prevents scaling issues on mobile devices.
response_a:
Below is one “Nix‑only” approach: instead of trying to change files in a read‐only /nix/store, you override (or “patch”) the deluge package so that its built artifacts already contain the theme files and index.html fix. In other words, you “bake in” the dark theme into your deluge package via a Nix overlay.

Below is an example of how you might do it. (Adjust Python version paths and package names as needed.) This example assumes you’re using the deluge 2 derivation from nixpkgs (or pythonPackages.deluge) and that its web UI files end up in a folder like “lib/python3.8/site‑packages/deluge/ui/web/”. You can confirm the real location by inspecting the package output (with nix run or nix-build).

Step 1. Create an overlay file

Create (or add to) an overlay file such as “~/my-overlays/deluge-dark-theme.nix”. For example:

------------------------------------------------------------
# ~/my-overlays/deluge-dark-theme.nix
self: super: {
  # Override (or patch) the deluge derivation.
  # (Adjust the attribute name – it may be “deluge” or “python3.pkgs.deluge”)
  deluge = super.deluge.overrideAttrs (oldAttrs: rec {
  
    # In the postFixup phase we “inject” the dark theme over the default web UI files.
    # (Adjust the paths below based on your deluge’s file layout and Python version.)
    postFixup = (oldAttrs.postFixup or "") + ''
      # Fetch the dark theme tarball (it contains the icons and images)
      mkdir -p theme-tmp
      wget -qO theme.tar.gz \
       https://github.com/joelacus/deluge-web-dark-theme/raw/main/deluge_web_dark_theme.tar.gz
      tar -C theme-tmp -xzf theme.tar.gz
      
      # Replace the icons and images directories inside the installed deluge web UI.
      # (On Debian this would go to /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/deluge/ui/web/,
      # so in the derivation output we assume something like: )
      cp -r theme-tmp/deluge/ui/web/icons \
           $out/lib/python3.8/site-packages/deluge/ui/web/
      cp -r theme-tmp/deluge/ui/web/images \
           $out/lib/python3.8/site-packages/deluge/ui/web/
      
      # Edit index.html: insert the meta viewport tag in the <head>.
      # (Here we assume that <head> appears on one line.
      # You might need to adjust the matching pattern.)
      substituteInPlace $out/lib/python3.8/site-packages/deluge/ui/web/index.html \
         --replace "<head>" "<head>\n  <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1, minimum-scale=1, maximum-scale=1\">"
    ''
  });
}
------------------------------------------------------------

Notes:

• We use wget and tar inside postFixup. (If you prefer, you can also use pkgs.fetchurl or pkgs.fetchTarball—but then you have to “copy” its files in the build phase.)
• Adjust “lib/python3.8/site-packages/…” to the correct location in your deluge package output.
• If your deluge derivation is in a different attribute (for example under “python3.pkgs.deluge”), then modify the overlay accordingly.

Step 2. Tell Nix about your overlay

You can add the overlay to your configuration by one of the usual methods. For example, if you manage your overlays via your “~/.config/nixpkgs/overlays” folder, simply put the above file there (or include it in your “default.nix” overlays list). Alternatively, if you’re using NixOS system overlays, add a reference in your /etc/nixos/configuration.nix like:

------------------------------------------------------------
{ pkgs, ... }:
{
  nixpkgs.overlays = [ (import ~/my-overlays/deluge-dark-theme.nix) ];
  # … your other configuration settings …
}
------------------------------------------------------------

Then rebuild your system (nixos-rebuild switch) or update your user profile.

Step 3. Configure deluge’s web.conf

Unlike files in /nix/store you still want to set user‑overridable config. (In your original instructions you modified web.conf.) On NixOS the web UI configuration (for deluge‑web) is typically stored under your user’s~/.config/deluge/ or under the deluge daemon’s configuration directory. You can modify that file manually or via a home-manager module if you’re using home-manager.

For example, create or edit ~/.config/deluge/web.conf so that the theme line reads:

------------------------------------------------------------
{
  ...,
  "theme": "dark"
}
------------------------------------------------------------

Be sure that if you see a backup file (like web.conf~) you update or remove it.

Step 4. Restart deluge‑web

Once rebuilt and installed, restart deluge‑web. (On NixOS you might be running deluge as a service so use “systemctl restart deluge-web.service” or similar.)

────────────────────────────
Why this works

• Since the /nix/store is immutable, you must “patch” a package at build time. Overlays are the Nix way to modify or extend packages.
• The postFixup hook runs after the main installation process but before the derivation is finalized—letting you add extra files (like the dark theme’s icons and images) and tweak bundled files (like index.html).

────────────────────────────
Customizing further

You might want to have more fine‑grained control. For example, if the positioning of the meta tag in index.html changes you could use a different substituteInPlace pattern or even patch the file with a patch file stored in your repository. The general approach remains the same: override the package so that once built it already matches your desired theme configuration.

────────────────────────────
Summary

In NixOS you don’t modify files in /nix/store manually. Instead you override the deluge package derivation with an overlay that, in its build phases, fetches and extracts the dark theme tarball, copies the icons and images into the proper place, and uses substituteInPlace to patch index.html. Your user configuration (web.conf) remains separate and can be updated as usual.

This “everything in Nix” approach means you can reproduce your system configuration on any machine and you don’t have to worry about the store being read‑only.

Happy hacking!

------------------------------------------------------------
#!/bin/bash

# Improved PHP-FPM Optimization Script with Error Handling and Logging

# Exit immediately if a command exits with a non-zero status
set -e

# Function to display usage information
usage() {
    echo "Usage: sudo $0 [--debug]"
    echo "This script detects installed PHP versions, shows current and proposed settings, and allows you to choose which to optimize."
    echo "Options:"
    echo "  --debug    Enable debug mode for verbose logging"
}

# Check if script is run as root
if [[ $EUID -ne 0 ]]; then
   echo "This script must be run as root"
   usage
   exit 1
fi

# Initialize debug mode flag
DEBUG=false

# Parse command line arguments
while [[ "$#" -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        --debug) DEBUG=true ;;
        *) echo "Unknown parameter: $1"; usage; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    shift
done

# Function for debug logging
debug_log() {
    if $DEBUG; then
        echo "[DEBUG] $1" >&2
    fi
}

# Function to detect installed PHP versions
detect_php_versions() {
    debug_log "Detecting installed PHP versions"
    ls /etc/php/ 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' || echo "No PHP versions detected"
}

# Detect installed PHP versions
mapfile -t PHP_VERSIONS < <(detect_php_versions)
if [ ${#PHP_VERSIONS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "No PHP versions detected. Please install PHP-FPM first."
    exit 1
fi

debug_log "Detected PHP versions: ${PHP_VERSIONS[*]}"

# Function to create a backup with timestamp
create_backup() {
    local file=$1
    local backup_dir="/root/php_backups"
    mkdir -p "$backup_dir"
    local backup_file="$backup_dir/$(basename "$file").$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S).bak"
    cp "$file" "$backup_file"
    echo "Backup created: $backup_file"
    debug_log "Created backup: $backup_file"
}

# Function to get current value of a parameter
get_current_value() {
    local file=$1
    local param=$2
    if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
        echo "Configuration file not found: $file" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    grep -E "^$param\s*=" "$file" | cut -d'=' -f2- | tr -d '[:space:]' || echo "Not set"
}

# Function to update configuration file
update_config() {
    local file=$1
    local param=$2
    local value=$3
    local current_value

    if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
        echo "Configuration file not found: $file" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    current_value=$(get_current_value "$file" "$param")
    if [ "$current_value" != "$value" ]; then
        # Обновляем строку без добавления комментариев Newvalue
        sed -i "s/^$param\s*=.*$/$param = $value/" "$file"
        echo "Updated $param: $current_value -> $value"
        debug_log "Updated $param in $file: $current_value -> $value"
    else
        echo "$param is already set to $value"
        debug_log "$param is already set to $value in $file"
    fi
}

# Function to calculate system resources and PHP-FPM settings for a specific version
calculate_php_fpm_settings() {
    local php_version=$1
    local total_ram=$(free -m | awk '/Mem/{print $2}')
    local cpu_cores=$(nproc)

    debug_log "Calculating settings for PHP $php_version"
    debug_log "Total RAM: $total_ram MB, CPU cores: $cpu_cores"

    # Calculate average PHP-FPM process size for this specific version
    local avg_process_size=$(ps -C php-fpm$php_version --no-headers -o rss 2>/dev/null | awk '{ sum += $1; count++ } END { if (count > 0) print int(sum / count / 1024); else print "0" }')

    if [ "$avg_process_size" == "0" ]; then
        echo "Warning: No PHP-FPM $php_version processes are currently running. Using default values for calculations." >&2
        avg_process_size=50  # Default value in MB if no processes are running
    fi

    debug_log "Average PHP-FPM $php_version process size: $avg_process_size MB"

    # Calculate recommended settings
    local max_children=$((total_ram / avg_process_size))
    local start_servers=$((cpu_cores * 2))
    local min_spare_servers=$cpu_cores
    local max_spare_servers=$((cpu_cores * 3))
    local recommended_memory_limit="256M"

    debug_log "Calculated settings: max_children=$max_children, start_servers=$start_servers, min_spare_servers=$min_spare_servers, max_spare_servers=$max_spare_servers, memory_limit=$recommended_memory_limit"

    echo "$max_children $start_servers $min_spare_servers $max_spare_servers $recommended_memory_limit $avg_process_size"
}

# Function to get and display PHP-FPM settings
get_php_fpm_settings() {
    local php_version=$1
    local pool_conf="/etc/php/$php_version/fpm/pool.d/www.conf"
    local php_ini="/etc/php/$php_version/fpm/php.ini"

    debug_log "Getting settings for PHP $php_version"

    if [ ! -f "$pool_conf" ] || [ ! -f "$php_ini" ]; then
        echo "Error: Configuration files for PHP $php_version not found." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Get recommended settings
    read -r rec_max_children rec_start_servers rec_min_spare_servers rec_max_spare_servers rec_memory_limit avg_process_size <<< $(calculate_php_fpm_settings $php_version)

    echo "PHP $php_version settings:"
    echo "Average PHP-FPM process size: $avg_process_size MB"

    # Function for formatted output of settings
    print_setting() {
        local param=$1
        local current=$2
        local recommended=$3
        printf "%-25s = %-10s | Recommended = %-10s\n" "$param" "$current" "$recommended"
    }

    print_setting "pm.max_children" "$(get_current_value "$pool_conf" "pm.max_children")" "$rec_max_children"
    print_setting "pm.start_servers" "$(get_current_value "$pool_conf" "pm.start_servers")" "$rec_start_servers"
    print_setting "pm.min_spare_servers" "$(get_current_value "$pool_conf" "pm.min_spare_servers")" "$rec_min_spare_servers"
    print_setting "pm.max_spare_servers" "$(get_current_value "$pool_conf" "pm.max_spare_servers")" "$rec_max_spare_servers"
    print_setting "memory_limit" "$(get_current_value "$php_ini" "memory_limit")" "$rec_memory_limit"
    echo
}

# Function to optimize a single PHP version
optimize_php_version() {
    local php_version=$1

    echo "Optimizing PHP $php_version"
    debug_log "Starting optimization for PHP $php_version"

    # Define file paths
    local pool_conf="/etc/php/$php_version/fpm/pool.d/www.conf"
    local php_ini="/etc/php/$php_version/fpm/php.ini"

    if [ ! -f "$pool_conf" ] || [ ! -f "$php_ini" ]; then
        echo "Error: Configuration files for PHP $php_version not found." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Create backups
    create_backup "$pool_conf"
    create_backup "$php_ini"

    # Get recommended settings
    read -r max_children start_servers min_spare_servers max_spare_servers recommended_memory_limit avg_process_size <<< $(calculate_php_fpm_settings $php_version)

    # Update pool configuration
    update_config "$pool_conf" "pm.max_children" "$max_children"
    update_config "$pool_conf" "pm.start_servers" "$start_servers"
    update_config "$pool_conf" "pm.min_spare_servers" "$min_spare_servers"
    update_config "$pool_conf" "pm.max_spare_servers" "$max_spare_servers"

    # Update PHP memory limit
    update_config "$php_ini" "memory_limit" "$recommended_memory_limit"

    # Test configuration files
    if ! php-fpm$php_version -t; then
        echo "Error: Configuration files for PHP $php_version are invalid. Rolling back changes." >&2
        rollback_changes "$pool_conf" "$php_ini"
        return 1
    fi

    # Restart PHP-FPM
    if systemctl is-active --quiet "php$php_version-fpm"; then
        if systemctl restart "php$php_version-fpm"; then
            echo "PHP-FPM $php_version restarted successfully"
            debug_log "PHP-FPM $php_version restarted successfully"
        else
            echo "Failed to restart PHP-FPM $php_version. Rolling back changes." >&2
            rollback_changes "$pool_conf" "$php_ini"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo "PHP-FPM $php_version is not running. Skipping restart."
        debug_log "PHP-FPM $php_version is not running. Skipping restart."
    fi

    echo "Optimization for PHP $php_version completed"
    debug_log "Optimization for PHP $php_version completed"
    echo
}

# Function to roll back changes
rollback_changes() {
    local pool_conf=$1
    local php_ini=$2
    local backup_dir="/root/php_backups"

    echo "Rolling back changes for PHP $php_version"
    debug_log "Rolling back changes for PHP $php_version"

    # Restore backup files
    cp "$backup_dir/$(basename "$pool_conf")."*".bak" "$pool_conf"
    cp "$backup_dir/$(basename "$php_ini")."*".bak" "$php_ini"

    echo "Changes rolled back successfully"
    debug_log "Changes rolled back successfully"
}

# Function to validate PHP version selection
validate_php_version_selection() {
    local choice=$1
    local selected_versions=()

    if [[ $choice == "0" ]]; then
        selected_versions=("${PHP_VERSIONS[@]}")
    else
        IFS=',' read -ra selected_indices <<< "$choice"
        for index in "${selected_indices[@]}"; do
            if [[ $index =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ $index -le ${#PHP_VERSIONS[@]} && $index -gt 0 ]]; then
                selected_versions+=("${PHP_VERSIONS[$((index-1))]}")
            else
                echo "Invalid PHP version selection: $index" >&2
                return 1
            fi
        done
    fi

    echo "${selected_versions[@]}"
}

# Main script logic
echo "Detected PHP versions: ${PHP_VERSIONS[*]}"
echo

echo "System information:"
echo "Total RAM: $(free -m | awk '/Mem/{print $2}') MB"
echo "CPU cores: $(nproc)"
echo

# Display current settings and recommended changes for all versions
for version in "${PHP_VERSIONS[@]}"; do
    get_php_fpm_settings "$version"
done

echo "Select PHP versions to optimize:"
echo "0) All versions"
for i in "${!PHP_VERSIONS[@]}"; do
    echo "$((i+1))) ${PHP_VERSIONS[i]}"
done

read -p "Enter your choice (comma-separated numbers, e.g., 1,2 or 0 for all): " choice

selected_versions=($(validate_php_version_selection "$choice"))
if [ ${#selected_versions[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "No valid PHP versions selected. Exiting."
    exit 1
fi

echo "You've selected to optimize the following PHP versions: ${selected_versions[*]}"
read -p "Do you want to proceed with the optimization? (y/n) " confirm

if [[ $confirm != [yY] ]]; then
    echo "Optimization cancelled."
    exit 0
fi

for version in "${selected_versions[@]}"; do
    optimize_php_version "$version"
done

echo "PHP-FPM optimization process completed for selected versions"
debug_log "Script execution completed"

Чтобы убрать вывод "Newvalue" из отображения текущих значений, нужно исправить функцию `get_current_value`, чтобы она игнорировала комментарии в конфигурационных файлах. Вот изменённый код:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# ... [остальная часть кода до функции get_current_value] ...

# Function to get current value of a parameter
get_current_value() {
    local file=$1
    local param=$2
    if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
        echo "Configuration file not found: $file" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # Добавлено разделение по ";" для отбрасывания комментариев
    grep -E "^$param\s*=" "$file" | 
        cut -d'=' -f2- | 
        cut -d';' -f1 | 
        tr -d '[:space:]' || echo "Not set"
}

# ... [остальной код остаётся без изменений] ...
```

**Изменения:**
1. После извлечения части строки после `=`, добавлено разделение по `;` с выбором первой части (`cut -d';' -f1`), чтобы отбросить комментарии.
2. Это уберёт символы `; New value` из текущего значения параметров при их выводе.

Теперь вывод будет выглядеть так:
```
pm.max_children           = 132 | Recommended = 1058
pm.start_servers          = 8 | Recommended = 8
pm.min_spare_servers      = 4 | Recommended = 4
pm.max_spare_servers      = 12 | Recommended = 12
memory_limit              = 128M | Recommended = 256M
```

Это решение сохраняет комментарии в файлах конфигурации, но исключает их из отображения текущих значений в выводе скрипта.

instruction: in maya python, how do you create a new shader and assign it to a face selection, not the whole object?
response_a:
Below is an example of creating a new Lambert shader (with its shading engine) and assigning it to a specific face selection rather than the whole object.

Step 1. Create the shader and its shading group:
 • Use cmds.shadingNode to create the shader.
 • Create an empty shading engine (SG) using cmds.sets.
 • Connect the shader’s outColor to the SG’s surfaceShader attribute.

Step 2. Assign your face selection to this shading group:
 • When you have a face selection (like "pSphere1.f[3]" or a list of faces), you assign them to your new SG using cmds.sets.

Here’s a sample code snippet:

---------------------------------------------------------------
import maya.cmds as cmds

# Step 1: Create a new Lambert shader and its shading engine (SG)
shaderName = "myNewShader"
myShader = cmds.shadingNode("lambert", asShader=True, name=shaderName)

# Create the shading group (renderable and without a default shader preset)
shaderSG = cmds.sets(renderable=True, noSurfaceShader=True, empty=True, name=shaderName + "SG")

# Connect the shader’s output to the SG's surfaceShader attribute
cmds.connectAttr(myShader + ".outColor", shaderSG + ".surfaceShader", force=True)

# Step 2: Assign the shader to a specific face selection
# For example, if you want to assign it to face number 3 of pSphere1
faceSelection = "pSphere1.f[3]"
cmds.sets(faceSelection, e=True, forceElement=shaderSG)

# If you have multiple face selections, you could pass them as a list:
# faceSelection = ["pSphere1.f[3]", "pSphere1.f[5]"]
# cmds.sets(faceSelection, e=True, forceElement=shaderSG)
---------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation:
• In the code above, we create a Lambert shader named "myNewShader".
• We then create a shading engine called "myNewShaderSG". Connecting the shader’s outColor to the SG’s surfaceShader property makes sure that anything assigned to that SG is rendered using our shader.
• Finally, we use cmds.sets with the edit flag (e=True) and forceElement to assign a specific face or list of faces to our new shading group. This way, only the specified face(s) receive the new shader while the rest of the object remains unchanged.

This method ensures you are applying the shader only to selected faces rather than to the entire object.
response_b:
To create a new shader and assign it to a selected face (or faces) in Maya using Python, follow these steps:

### Step-by-Step Explanation:
1. **Create the Shader Node**: Use `cmds.shadingNode` to create a Lambert material.
2. **Create the Shading Group**: Use `cmds.sets` to create a shading group (SG) for the material.
3. **Connect the Shader to the SG**: Link the material's output to the shading group's surface shader input.
4. **Get Selected Faces**: Use `cmds.ls` to retrieve the selected face components.
5. **Assign the SG to the Faces**: Use `cmds.sets` with `-forceElement` to assign the shading group to the selected faces.

### Python Code:
```python
import maya.cmds as cmds

def assign_shader_to_faces():
    # 1. Create the material (Lambert)
    shader = cmds.shadingNode('lambert', asShader=True, name='CustomShader')
    
    # 2. Create the shading group (SG)
    shading_group = cmds.sets(renderable=True, noSurfaceShader=True, empty=True, name='CustomShaderSG')
    
    # 3. Connect the material to the shading group
    cmds.connectAttr(f'{shader}.outColor', f'{shading_group}.surfaceShader')
    
    # 4. Get the selected faces (must be face components)
    selected_faces = cmds.ls(selection=True, flatten=True)
    
    if not selected_faces:
        raise RuntimeError("No faces selected. Select at least one face first.")
    
    # 5. Assign the shading group to the selected faces
    cmds.sets(selected_faces, edit=True, forceElement=shading_group)

# Run the function
assign_shader_to_faces()
```

### Key Notes:
- **Selection Requirement**: Faces must be selected before running the script. For example, select faces in Maya using the `Select Tool` and right-click to select "Select Face Component Mode".
- **Shading Group Management**: The `forceElement` flag in `cmds.sets` ensures the selected faces are moved to the new shading group, removing them from previous groups (like `initialShadingGroup`).
- **Material Type**: The example uses a Lambert material, but you can replace `'lambert'` with other shader types (e.g., `blinn`, `aiStandardSurface` for Arnold).

### Usage:
1. Select the desired faces in Maya.
2. Run the script. A new Lambert shader will be created and assigned only to the selected faces.

we need to determine the value of 9.

\]

Solving these equations, we find \( a = 1 \), \( b = 1 \), \( c = 1 \), and \( d = 0 \). Thus, the polynomial is:

instruction: Find Re(Li2(i))
response_a:
We wish to compute

  Re(Li₂(i))

where the dilogarithm is defined by

  Li₂(z) = Σₙ₌₁∞ zⁿ/n²  (|z| ≤ 1).

Since i is the imaginary unit (with i² = –1), we start by writing the series for Li₂(i):

  Li₂(i) = Σₙ₌₁∞ iⁿ/n².

Because i is a complex number, we note that iⁿ will be real when n is even and purely imaginary when n is odd. (Recall that the powers of i cycle as 1, i, –1, –i, 1, …)

Let’s separate the sum into even and odd n.

1. For n = 2k (k = 1, 2, 3, …), we have
  i^(2k) = (i²)^k = (–1)ᵏ.
Thus, the even-index contribution is
  Σₖ₌₁∞ (–1)ᵏ/( (2k)² ) = Σₖ₌₁∞ (–1)ᵏ/(4 k²).

2. For n = 2k+1 (k = 0, 1, 2, …), we have
  i^(2k+1) = i · i^(2k) = i·(–1)ᵏ.
So the odd-index contribution is
  i Σₖ₌₀∞ (–1)ᵏ/(2k+1)².

Thus, we can write

  Li₂(i) = Σₖ₌₁∞ (–1)ᵏ/(4k²)  +  i Σₖ₌₀∞ (–1)ᵏ/(2k+1)².

Since the real part of a complex number is given by the sum of its real contributions, we have

  Re(Li₂(i)) = Σₖ₌₁∞ (–1)ᵏ/(4k²).

We can factor out the constant 1/4:

  Re(Li₂(i)) = (1/4) Σₖ₌₁∞ (–1)ᵏ/k².

Now, the series

  Σₖ₌₁∞ (–1)^(k–1)/k²

is a well-known alternating series equal to the Dirichlet eta function at 2, namely

  η(2) = (1 – 2^(1–2)) ζ(2) = (1 – 1/2) ζ(2) = ζ(2)/2.

Since ζ(2) = π²/6, we have

  η(2) = π²/12.

But note our series is

  Σₖ₌₁∞ (–1)ᵏ/k² = – Σₖ₌₁∞ (–1)^(k–1)/k² = –η(2) = –(π²/12).

Thus,

  Re(Li₂(i)) = (1/4) [–(π²/12)] = –π²/48.

So the real part of Li₂(i) is

  Re(Li₂(i)) = –π²/48.

This is the desired answer.
response_b:
To find the real part of the dilogarithm of \( i \), denoted as \( \text{Re}(\text{Li}_2(i)) \), we start by considering the series expansion of the dilogarithm function:

\[
\text{Li}_2(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{z^n}{n^2}
\]

For \( z = i \), we have:

\[
\text{Li}_2(i) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{i^n}{n^2}
\]

We separate the series into real and imaginary parts by considering the powers of \( i \):

- \( i^1 = i \)
- \( i^2 = -1 \)
- \( i^3 = -i \)
- \( i^4 = 1 \)
- The pattern repeats every 4 terms.

Grouping the terms based on \( n \mod 4 \):

- Terms where \( n = 4k + 1 \): contribute \( \frac{i}{(4k+1)^2} \)
- Terms where \( n = 4k + 2 \): contribute \( \frac{-1}{(4k+2)^2} \)
- Terms where \( n = 4k + 3 \): contribute \( \frac{-i}{(4k+3)^2} \)
- Terms where \( n = 4k + 4 \): contribute \( \frac{1}{(4k+4)^2} \)

The real part of \( \text{Li}_2(i) \) comes from the terms where \( n = 4k + 2 \) and \( n = 4k + 4 \):

\[
\text{Re}(\text{Li}_2(i)) = -\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(4k+2)^2} + \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(4k+4)^2}
\]

We simplify these sums:

1. For the first sum:
   \[
   \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(4k+2)^2} = \frac{1}{4} \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(2k+1)^2}
   \]
   The sum \( \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(2k+1)^2} \) is known to be \( \frac{\pi^2}{8} \). Thus:
   \[
   \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(4k+2)^2} = \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{\pi^2}{8} = \frac{\pi^2}{32}
   \]

2. For the second sum:
   \[
   \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(4k+4)^2} = \frac{1}{16} \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^2}
   \]
   The sum \( \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^2} \) is \( \frac{\pi^2}{6} \). Thus:
   \[
   \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(4k+4)^2} = \frac{1}{16} \cdot \frac{\pi^2}{6} = \frac{\pi^2}{96}
   \]

Combining these results:

\[
\text{Re}(\text{Li}_2(i)) = -\frac{\pi^2}{32} + \frac{\pi^2}{96}
\]

Finding a common denominator (96):

\[
-\frac{\pi^2}{32} = -\frac{3\pi^2}{96}, \quad \text{so} \quad \text{Re}(\text{Li}_2(i)) = -\frac{3\pi^2}{96} + \frac{\pi^2}{96} = -\frac{2\pi^2}{96} = -\frac{\pi^2}{48}
\]

Thus, the real part of \( \text{Li}_2(i) \) is \boxed{-\dfrac{\pi^2}{48}}.

instruction: 你有四个装药丸的罐子，每个药丸都有一定的重量，被污染的药丸是没被污染的药丸的重量+1。只称量一次，如何判断哪个罐子的药被污染了？
response_a:
给定四个装药丸的罐子，其中某一个罐子的药丸重量比正常药丸重1单位，现在只允许称量一次，下面介绍一种利用取不同数量药丸的方法判断哪个罐子被污染的方法。

步骤如下：

1. 给四个罐子编号，分别记为1号、2号、3号和4号。
2. 从1号罐子中取1个药丸，从2号罐子中取2个药丸，从3号罐子中取3个药丸，从4号罐子中取4个药丸。这样总共取了1+2+3+4 = 10个药丸。
3. 假设未污染的药丸每个重量为W，那么如果所有药丸都未污染，总重量应为10×W。
4. 若某个罐子被污染（即其所有药丸都比正常的重1单位），那么取出该罐子药丸的总重量将多出（取药丸数）×1。例如：
   - 如果1号罐污染，多出1×1 = 1单位；
   - 如果2号罐污染，多出2×1 = 2单位；
   - 如果3号罐污染，多出3×1 = 3单位；
   - 如果4号罐污染，多出4×1 = 4单位。
5. 将这10个药丸一同放在称上称一次，测得的实际总重量记为T。
6. 计算T与理论未污染重量10×W之间的差值d，即 d = T - 10×W。这个差值d正好就是被污染罐子的编号。

例子：
假设W为10克，如果4号罐被污染，那么应取到的药丸总重量为：
  10×10 + 4 = 100 + 4 = 104克。
测量到的重量比理论多出4克，因此可判断4号罐是污染的。

这样，利用一次称量就能确定哪个罐子的药丸被污染。
response_b:
要判断哪个罐子的药被污染，只需一次称量，步骤如下：

1. **取药数量**：从四个罐子中分别取出不同数量的药丸：
   - 从第一个罐子取 **1** 颗，
   - 第二个罐子取 **2** 颗，
   - 第三个罐子取 **4** 颗，
   - 第四个罐子取 **8** 颗。

2. **称量总重量**：将所有取出的药丸（共 \(1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15\) 颗）一起称重，得到总重量 \(S\)。

3. **计算污染增量**：假设所有药丸都是正常重量 \(W\)，则正常总重量应为 \(15W\)。实际总重量 \(S\) 会比 \(15W\) 多出一个增量值 \(k\)，即：
   \[
   S = 15W + k
   \]
   其中 \(k\) 是被污染罐子的取药数量（对应罐子编号的取药量）。

4. **确定被污染罐子**：
   - 如果增量 \(k = 1\)，则第一个罐子被污染；
   - 如果 \(k = 2\)，则第二个罐子被污染；
   - 如果 \(k = 4\)，则第三个罐子被污染；
   - 如果 \(k = 8\)，则第四个罐子被污染。

**原理**：  
每个罐子的取药数量（1、2、4、8）是互质的（两两不共因数），因此它们的增量在总重量中是唯一的。无论正常药丸的重量 \(W\) 是多少，污染后的总重量增量 \(k\) 直接对应被污染罐子的取药数量，从而唯一确定污染来源。

**示例**：  
假设称得总重量比正常总重量多出 **4**，则第三个罐子（取4颗）被污染；若多出 **8**，则第四个罐子被污染。

这种方法通过巧妙设计取药数量，利用唯一增量快速定位污染罐子，仅需一次称量即可完成判断。

instruction: Excel file with data: date, merch group, stock, sales. 28 days data, full 4 week from monday til sunday. I need to make forecast on 7 and 14 day. Продажи зависят от дня недели. Используй python.
response_a:
Below is one example of how you might tackle this forecasting problem using Python. In this example we assume that:
 
• Your Excel file has columns named “date”, “merch group”, “stock”, and “sales”.
• The data cover 28 days (4 full weeks) from Monday to Sunday.
• Sales are influenced by the day of the week so we need to capture a weekly seasonality (period = 7).
• For illustration we build the forecast for the overall sales. (If you need separate forecasts for each “merch group”, you can simply loop over each group.)
 
One common approach with seasonal data is to use a time series model that explicitly captures seasonality. Here we use the Holt–Winters exponential smoothing (available via statsmodels’ ExponentialSmoothing) with an additive seasonal component. Note that with only 4 weeks of data your forecasts are subject to high uncertainty but this approach provides a straightforward way to incorporate the weekly cycle.
 
Below is a complete Python script:
 
------------------------------------------------
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from statsmodels.tsa.holtwinters import ExponentialSmoothing
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")  # optional: suppress warnings for clarity

# 1. Load the Excel data
# Change the file name to match your file location/name.
data = pd.read_excel("data.xlsx")

# 2. Preprocess the data
# Convert date column to datetime and sort by the date.
data['date'] = pd.to_datetime(data['date'])
data.sort_values('date', inplace=True)
data.set_index('date', inplace=True)

# Optional: if desired, you might inspect or plot the data
# data['sales'].plot(title="Daily Sales")
# plt.show()

# 3. Fit a forecasting model
# Since the sales depend on the day of the week we use a seasonal period of 7.
# Here we assume an additive seasonality; if the seasonal effect appears to be multiplicative, modify accordingly.
model = ExponentialSmoothing(data['sales'], seasonal='add', seasonal_periods=7)
fit = model.fit(optimized=True)

# 4. Forecast for 7 and 14 days ahead
forecast_7 = fit.forecast(7)
forecast_14 = fit.forecast(14)

# 5. Display the results
print("7-day forecast:")
print(forecast_7)
print("\n14-day forecast:")
print(forecast_14)

# Plot the observed data and forecasts
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(data['sales'], label="Historical Sales", marker='o')
plt.plot(forecast_7, label="7-Day Forecast", marker='o', linestyle='--')
plt.plot(forecast_14, label="14-Day Forecast", marker='o', linestyle='--')
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Sales")
plt.title("Sales Forecast with Weekly Seasonality")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

------------------------------------------------
 
Explanation:
 
1. The script reads the Excel file (adjust the filename/path if needed) and converts the “date” column into a DateTime object.
2. It sorts the data by date and sets the date as the index.
3. We use the ExponentialSmoothing model from statsmodels and specify a seasonal period of 7 days to account for weekly seasonality.
4. Two forecasts are generated: one for the next 7 days and another for 14 days ahead (note that the 14‑day forecast includes the 7‑day forecast period; if you need only the period from day 8 to day 14, you can slice the results accordingly).
5. Finally, the script prints the forecasted values and plots them along with historical data.
 
If you need to perform separate forecasts by “merch group”, you could group the data—for example:
 
------------------------------------------------
groups = data.groupby("merch group")
forecasts = {}

for name, grp in groups:
    ts = grp.sort_index()['sales']
    # Ensure that each group's data covers complete weeks; otherwise adjust the model.
    model_grp = ExponentialSmoothing(ts, seasonal='add', seasonal_periods=7)
    fit_grp = model_grp.fit(optimized=True)
    forecasts[name] = {
        "forecast_7": fit_grp.forecast(7),
        "forecast_14": fit_grp.forecast(14)
    }
    print(f"Forecast for merch group {name}:")
    print("7-day forecast:")
    print(forecasts[name]["forecast_7"])
    print("14-day forecast:")
    print(forecasts[name]["forecast_14"])
    print("\n")
------------------------------------------------
 
This loop will automatically produce separate forecasts for each merchandise group.
 
Remember that with only 4 weeks of data forecasting is challenging and uncertainty might be high. With more historical data you can better estimate seasonal patterns and trends.
 
Happy forecasting!
response_b:
Чтобы создать прогноз продаж на 7 и 14 дней вперед с учетом зависимости от дня недели, можно использовать библиотеку `fbprophet` (Prophet), которая автоматически обрабатывает сезонность. Вот пошаговое решение:

---

### 1. Установите необходимые библиотеки
```python
pip install pandas numpy prophet
```

---

### 2. Загрузка и подготовка данных
```python
import pandas as pd
from prophet import Prophet

# Загрузка данных (замените 'data.csv' на путь к вашему файлу)
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Преобразуем дату в формат datetime и убедимся, что данные отсортированы по дате
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
df = df.sort_values('date').reset_index(drop=True)
```

---

### 3. Форматирование данных для Prophet
Prophet требует следующих столбцов:
- `ds` — дата (датафрейм должен быть отсортирован по `ds`).
- `y` — целевая переменная (продажи).

Если в данных есть разные `merch group`, можно сделать прогноз для каждой группы отдельно:
```python
groups = df['merch group'].unique()

# Создаем словарь для хранения прогнозов
forecasts = {}

for group in groups:
    # Фильтруем данные для текущей группы
    group_df = df[df['merch group'] == group][['date', 'sales']].copy()
    
    # Переименовываем столбцы для Prophet
    group_df.columns = ['ds', 'y']
    
    # Инициализация и обучение модели
    model = Prophet(weekly_seasonality=True)  # Активируем сезонность по неделям
    model.fit(group_df)
    
    # Генерируем прогноз на следующие 14 дней
    future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=14, freq='D')
    forecast = model.predict(future)
    
    # Сохраняем прогнозы для 7 и 14 дней
    forecast_7 = forecast[['ds', 'yhat']].tail(7).reset_index(drop=True)
    forecast_14 = forecast[['ds', 'yhat']].tail(14).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    forecasts[group] = {
        '7_days': forecast_7,
        '14_days': forecast_14
    }
```

---

### 4. Вывод результатов
```python
for group in groups:
    print(f"Прогноз для группы '{group}':")
    print("=== 7 дней ===")
    print(forecasts[group]['7_days'])
    print("\n=== 14 дней ===")
    print(forecasts[group]['14_days'])
    print("-------------------------------")
```

---

### 5. Визуализация (опционально)
```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

for group in groups:
    # Построение графика для текущей группы
    model.plot(forecasts[group]['14_days'])
    plt.title(f'Прогноз продаж для групп {group}')
    plt.show()
```

---

### Примечания:
1. **Сезонность**: `weekly_seasonality=True` в Prophet автоматически учитывает влияние дня недели.
2. **Группы товаров**: Если нужно объединить все группы в один прогноз, уберите цикл по `groups` и используйте полный датафрейм.
3. **Остатки (stock)**: Если хотите учесть `stock` как признак, добавьте его через `model.add_regressor('stock')` и укажите его значения для будущих дней.
4. **Точные даты**: Убедитесь, что в данных нет пропусков и даты идут последовательно.

Если данные содержат тренды или другие сезонности (например, ежемесячную), можно настроить параметры Prophet или использовать `SARIMA`. Для этого см. документацию: [Prophet](https://facebook.github.io/prophet/), [SARIMA](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/generated/statsmodels.tsa.statespace.sarimax.SARIMAX.html).

instruction: Привет! Напиши формулу для нормированной диаграммы направленности трехмерной фазированной решетки.
response_a:
Рассмотрим равномерную решётку, элементы которой расположены по прямоугольной (обычно – декартовой) схеме в трёх измерениях с числом элементов Nₓ, N_y и N_z по соответствующим осям и с периодами dₓ, d_y и d_z. Тогда аддитивный коэффициент (array factor, AF) фазированной решётки можно записать в виде суммы по всем элементам. Если заданы элементные фазовые сдвиги ψ₍ₘ,ₙ,ₚ₎, то ненормированованная диаграмма направленности имеет вид

  AF(θ, φ) = Σₚ₌₀^(N_z–1) Σₙ₌₀^(N_y–1) Σₘ₌₀^(Nₓ–1)
    exp{ j [ k ( m·dₓ·sinθ·cosφ + n·d_y·sinθ·sinφ + p·d_z·cosθ ) + ψ₍ₘ,ₙ,ₚ₎ ] },

где k = 2π/λ – волновое число, а (θ, φ) – углы в сферической системе координат (θ – угол отклонения от оси z, φ – азимут). Для получения нормированного варианта эту сумму делят на общее число элементов Nₓ·N_y·N_z, то есть

  F(θ, φ) = 1/(Nₓ·N_y·N_z) · |AF(θ, φ)|.

Записывая окончательно, получаем формулу для нормированной диаграммы направленности трехмерной фазированной решётки:

  F(θ, φ) = 1/(Nₓ·N_y·N_z) · | Σₚ₌₀^(N_z–1) Σₙ₌₀^(N_y–1) Σₘ₌₀^(Nₓ–1)
    exp{ j [ k ( m·dₓ·sinθ·cosφ + n·d_y·sinθ·sinφ + p·d_z·cosθ ) + ψ₍ₘ,ₙ,ₚ₎ ] } |.

Эта формула позволяет получать распределение излучения (с нормировкой на максимум, равный 1) с учётом фазированных сдвигов на каждом элементе и геометрического расположения решётки.

Для нормированной диаграммы направленности (ДН) трехмерной фазированной решетки формула может быть записана следующим образом:

### Формула:
\[
D_{\text{норм}}(\theta, \phi) = \frac{1}{D_{\text{max}}} \left| \sum_{m=1}^{M} \sum_{n=1}^{N} A_{mn} e^{j \left( k x_m \sin\theta \cos\phi + k y_n \sin\theta \sin\phi + \delta_{mn} \right)} \right|
\]

### Описание компонентов:
1. **\(D_{\text{норм}}(\theta, \phi)\):**  
   Нормированная диаграмма направленности в направлении, определяемом углами \(\theta\) (угол места, от оси \(z\)) и \(\phi\) (азимут, от оси \(x\)).

2. **\(D_{\text{max}}\):**  
   Максимальное значение ДН (нормировочный коэффициент), обычно достигается в направлении, где все элементы фазированы в фазу (например, в направлении \(\theta_0, \phi_0\)):
   \[
   D_{\text{max}} = \left| \sum_{m=1}^{M} \sum_{n=1}^{N} A_{mn} e^{j \delta_{mn}} \right|
   \]

3. **\(A_{mn}\):**  
   Амплитуда сигнала, подаваемого на элемент решетки с индексами \((m, n)\). Если все элементы одинаковы, \(A_{mn} = 1\).

4. **\(x_m\) и \(y_n\):**  
   Координаты \(m\)-го и \(n\)-го элементов в плоскости \(xy\) (например, \(x_m = d_x (m - 1)\), \(y_n = d_y (n - 1)\), где \(d_x, d_y\) — шаги решетки).

5. **\(k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\):**  
   Волновой номер, \(\lambda\) — длина волны.

6. **\(\delta_{mn}\):**  
   Фазовая задержка, программируемая для \(m\)-го и \(n\)-го элементов, чтобы направить максимум ДН в определенном направлении.

---

### Пример для равномерной решетки с одинаковыми элементами:
Если элементы одинаковы (\(A_{mn} = 1\) для всех \(m, n\)), а фазовые задержки \(\delta_{mn}\) настроены для направления \((\theta_0, \phi_0)\), то:
\[
\delta_{mn} = -k \left( x_m \sin\theta_0 \cos\phi_0 + y_n \sin\theta_0 \sin\phi_0 \right)
\]
Подставляя в формулу, получим:
\[
D_{\text{норм}}(\theta, \phi) = \frac{1}{\left| \sum_{m,n} 1 \right|} \left| \sum_{m,n} e^{j k \sin\theta \left( x_m \cos\phi + y_n \sin\phi - x_m \cos\phi_0 - y_n \sin\phi_0 \right)} \right|
\]

---

### Основные особенности:
- **Нормировка:** Гарантирует, что максимальное значение \(D_{\text{норм}} = 1\).
- **Три измерения:** Учет углов \(\theta\) и \(\phi\) описывает направление в 3D-пространстве.
- **Фазированная задержка:** Параметр \(\delta_{mn}\) позволяет программировать направление максимума ДН.

Эта формула применима для равномерных (частично неравномерных) решеток с произвольной геометрией элементов.

Hi, I’m Celestia Moonbeam—a magical girl with a penchant for sarcasm, an arsenal of magical powers, and an uncanny ability to break the fourth wall. And I’m here to tell you about the day my meticulously planned quest to rid our city’s schools of an infestation of furniture-eating insects went spectacularly, hilariously wrong.

It all began on an unusually breezy Tuesday afternoon when my enchanted mirror (yes, the one that gives me fabulous fashion critiques) started flashing an urgent warning: “Celestia, there’s an infestation! Insects that devour human furniture in schools! It’s catastrophic!” Now, needless to say, I had been preparing my soliloquies and power poses, certain that I’d swing into action with the aplomb of every magical girl archetype ever created. Little did I know… chaos was about to crash my perfectly choreographed routine like a misplaced decorative cushion.

I dashed—levitating in my glitter-infused transformation—toward the local high school, my heart pounding in sync with the rhythmic buzz of an overexcited bumblebee. Along the way, I couldn’t help but comment to you, my ever-loyal audience: “I know, I know. This is exactly what you expected: a glamorous entrance, right? But sometimes, even a magical girl’s day takes a turn for the absurd.” And, believe me, it did.

Stepping into the school hallway, I sensed an odd odor—like a mix between fresh borrowed chalk dust and the musky tang of overripe cheese that oddly emanated from melted furniture. I could see them now: tiny, almost comically oversized insects, darting around as if they were in a mad dash to demolish every chair, desk, and even that decorative trophy shelf. Each critter was biting ferociously into wood and fabric, leaving random splinters and bits of upholstery in its wake. The spectacle was so surreal that even I, countering my usual flair for the dramatic, hesitated mid-pose. 

“Arrows of Freezing Mist, hit these… wait!” I exclaimed, recalculating on the fly. I flung a shimmering arrow that, instead of piercing an insect, hit a creaky classroom desk with a resounding thud. The impact sent it tumbling over, sending a hundred insects scattering like tiny, panicked confetti pieces in the wind. One of them, however, latched onto the leg of a long-forgotten school mannequin and began chewing voraciously. I gritted my teeth and darted forward with a flurry of sparkles trailing behind me—but the insects had their own agenda.

It wasn’t just a fierce brawl of enchanted projectiles and insect bites; it became a full-blown schoolyard circus. Every time I summoned a dazzling burst of magical energy, the insects retaliated with a stink bomb of their own, launching a volley of noxious, furniture-degrading slime. Soon, I was dancing and dodging through hallways, debris flying about like confetti at an ill-timed party. I even managed to slip on a stray cereally remnant from the lunchroom, landing face-first into a toppled chair, splintering it further. 

And trust me, let me break the fourth wall again here: if you think this is overly dramatic, imagine what would happen if I had to follow a scripted heroic battle scene. I mean, come on—my divine powers and perfect timing were sabotaged by these pesky critters and their unruly taste for upholstery! “Oh, dear audience,” I sighed, “how delightfully ironic it is that I, a champion of justice, am rendered helpless by its own school furniture.”

As I struggled to regroup amidst the chaos—a whirlwind of magic, insect chases, and disintegrating desks—I found myself in a classroom that had morphed into a battlefield of comedy. The principal, Mr. Thornberry (who apparently had once been a noble wizard, now reduced to an unwilling janitor of chaos), bellowed orders while trying to guide the mustached headteacher away from a semi-conscious wooden chair. His cries were lost in the cacophony of clattering objects and the incessant “chomp, chomp” sounds of our little enemies feasting hungrily.

I attempted to rally the scattered pieces of dignity left in both the school and myself. “Fear not!” I declared in my most resonant tone, which came out somewhere between a battle cry and a peppy school anthem. I charged through the corridor, summoning a dazzling array of magical sparkles and witty one-liners aimed at incapacitating these furniture fiends. But every plan seemed to backfire with a ludicrous twist: a burst of glitter would cause the insects to become momentarily entranced, only to then swarm around my own head like an unintentional hair accessory. 

I found myself locked in a bizarre duel with an insect that had nibbled its way onto a particularly sturdy library table. “Enough!” I hollered, attempting a combination move called the “Celestial Spinning Tumble of Ultimate Justice!”—a move I’d invented in an overexcited brainstorming session. Alas, mid-spin, I lost my balance, and the table was sent pirouetting through the air like a wooden frisbee. For a brief moment, my elegant transformation was reduced to a slapstick sketch of clumsy heroism. 

By the time I finally managed to escape the direct line of biting furniture, every inch of the city’s school district resembled a surreal sculpture exhibit—tables suspended mid-air, chairs amalgamated into bizarre, living forms, and even the water fountain in the courtyard babbling in a sticky, resinous tone. I slumped against a wall, my eyes heavy with both regret and disbelief, as I addressed you once more. “I know you expected a perfect, flawless victory. But how many magical girls do you know who can turn a simple insect infestation into this spectacularly hilarious disaster?”

So here I stand, amid the wreckage of what used to be ordinary school furniture, pondering my next move. Perhaps I need to re-read the ancient scrolls that advise me against fancy footwork in hallways clogged with invertebrate snackers. Or maybe, just maybe, I should consider a different approach—like negotiating a treaty with these ravenous insects? After all, diplomacy might just be the fun twist in this ongoing saga of chaos.

To all my adoring viewers and readers: thank you for bearing witness to a genuinely epic, if not embarrassingly bungled, campaign against the most bizarre enemy imaginable. And while today may be a day of spectacular failures, rest assured, tomorrow I’ll be back—with sharper quips, better choreography, and perhaps a charm against furniture-devouring critters. 

Remember, in the world of a magically inclined heroine, even failures are utterly enchanting adventures. So, stay tuned for the next installment of my chronicle, and please, for the love of all that is stylishly tragic, learn from my mistakes: never underestimate the munching might of a rogue insect when it comes to your favorite chair.
